title: Arrow-correspondence geometry for comparing slice and fiber cones
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the relative join of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A\subseteq C$ be a full subcategory of a quasicategory, all small in one sufficiently large universe. Let $K\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ be the full subcategory on arrows $a\to c$ with $a\in A$, with source $\pi:K\to A$ and target $u:K\to C$. Then $K$ is a quasicategory and $u$ is a cocartesian fibration. For $c\in C$ its fiber $K_c$ is a quasicategory. Put $I_c=A\times_C C_{/c}$, where an $n$-simplex of $C_{/c}$ is $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to C$ ending at $c$, projected by the entire initial face. Then $I_c$ is a quasicategory, and the slice diagonal $\psi_c:I_c\to K_c$ is an equivalence: it sends $\sigma$ to the arrow prism obtained by precomposing with $[n]\times[1]\to[n+1]$, $(j,0)\mapsto j$, $(j,1)\mapsto n+1$. It respects the source projections exactly. For $a\in A$, the identity arrow $1_a$ is final in $K_a$.
Put $J=K\star_C C$. There is a functor $S:J\to C$ with $Si_K=\pi$ (followed by $A\subset C$), $Si_C=1_C$, and $Sj_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}=k_c$, where $k_c:I_c^{\triangleright}\to C$ appends $c$. The identity-arrow map $\delta:A\to K$ and the relative join map $\delta\star1$ give a coherent transformation $\beta:i_K\delta\to i_C|_A$ with $S\beta$ the constant transformation of $A\subset C$.
For each $c$ define $T_c^+=i_Ck_c$ and $T_c^-=j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}$. Let $b:I_c^{\triangleright}\to\Delta^1$ take the base to $0$ and apex to $1$. The map $(b,k_c)$ lands in $A\star_C C\subseteq\Delta^1\times C$. Define $T_c=(\delta\star1)(b,k_c)$. There exist coherent transformations $\gamma_c^+:T_c\to T_c^+$ and $\gamma_c^-:T_c\to T_c^-$. Both components at the apex are $1_{i_C(c)}$. At a base vertex $e:a\to c$, the component of $\gamma_c^+$ is $\beta_a$, while the component of $\gamma_c^-$ lies in $i_K(K)$ and is the arrow from $1_a$ to $e$ represented by the square with source side $1_a$ and target side $e$. Thus its image under $\pi$ is $1_a$. No limit, colimit, coefficient category or lifting theorem is asserted here.

proof.text:
By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the arrow simplicial set and its full subcategory $K$ are quasicategories. An inner-horn lifting problem for $u$ adjoints to a map from $(\Delta^1\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup(\{1\}\times\Delta^n)$ to $C$. Its inclusion in $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], applied to the inner horn inclusion and $\{1\}\subseteq\Delta^1$. The inner horn inclusion is inner anodyne by its defining lifting property. Since $C\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration, a filler exists. All source vertices belong to the given horn, hence lie in $A$; fullness puts the filler in $K$. Thus $u$ is an inner fibration. For $e:a\to c$ and $v:c\to c'$, fill the inner $2$-horn $(e,v)$, obtaining $h:a\to c'$ and its composition triangle. Together with the degenerate triangle at the source this gives a square, hence an edge $s:e\to h$ of $K$, with source side $1_a$ and target side $v$. Fix $z:b\to d$ in $K$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] and fullness, the mapping spaces from $e$ and $h$ to $z$ are respectively
$$\operatorname{Map}_C(a,b)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(a,d)}\operatorname{Map}_C(c,d),\qquad
\operatorname{Map}_C(a,b)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(a,d)}\operatorname{Map}_C(c',d).$$
The maps to the middle space are postcomposition with $z$ and precomposition with $e$ or $h$. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], precomposition depends only on component classes, is associative up to homotopy, and the composition triangle gives $[v][e]=[h]$, so $e^*v^*\simeq h^*$ on $\operatorname{Map}_C(c',d)$. Hence the composition triangle identifies the second space with the homotopy pullback of the first along $v^*:\operatorname{Map}_C(c',d)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(c,d)$: its data are a map $a\to b$, a map $c'\to d$, and a path between their composites $a\to d$, with all higher paths. One can eliminate the intermediate map $c\to d$ and its path to the composite with $v$, because the space of such choices with its specified path is contractible. Endpoint compatibility and naturality in the cited arrow-mapping theorem identify this pullback with the square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Therefore $s$ is $u$-cocartesian. The definition [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] now gives a cocartesian fibration. A horn in the strict fiber $K_c$ is a lifting problem for $u$ over the constant simplex at $c$; its filler stays in that fiber, so $K_c$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow correspondence; Corollary 5.3.7.3 (0478), with the mapping-space verification written out.

proof.text: Write $S_c=C_{/c}$ and $E_c=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_C\{c\}$. The prism formula and the equivalence $\delta_c:S_c\to E_c$ over $C$ are exactly [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. The source maps $S_c\to C$ and $E_c\to C$ are right fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to $\delta_c$: its map on each strict source fiber is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Pull back the two right fibrations and this map along $A\subseteq C$. Right-horn lifting is preserved by a degreewise pullback: compose a lifting square with $A\to C$, fill it in the original right fibration, and pair that filler with the given simplex in $A$. The resulting source fibers are unchanged. The fiberwise equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] gives a simplicial homotopy inverse over $A$ to the pulled-back map $\psi_c:I_c\to K_c$. Every vertex component of these homotopies is in a strict source fiber, hence in a Kan complex by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. All its edges are equivalences: the two outer $2$-horn fillers give inverse edges and their inverse triangles. Thus [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] turns the two homotopies into coherent natural equivalences, and $\psi_c$ is an equivalence of quasicategories. Both pullbacks are quasicategories, since they are full subcategories of $S_c,E_c$: a simplex lies in the pullback precisely when all its source vertices belong to $A$, equivalently its entire source face lies in $A$. The prism leaves that face unchanged, proving the exact equality of source projections. No assumption that $A$ is closed under equivalences of objects of $C$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, slice diagonal restriction; Theorem 4.6.4.19 and Corollary 4.6.4.20 (02VT).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final], the identity $1_a$ is final in $C_{/a}$. The source restriction $I_a$ is a full subcategory containing it. Its right-pinched mapping spaces into $1_a$ equal those in $C_{/a}$: every vertex of a defining mapping simplex is one of its two endpoints, so fullness includes every such simplex. They are therefore contractible, and $1_a$ is final in $I_a$. The equivalence $\psi_a$ of step 2 takes this vertex to the identity-arrow vertex of $K_a$. Equivalences induce equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Precomposition with an equivalence edge is a homotopy equivalence of mapping spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] (its component class is invertible, and composition is associative and unital up to homotopy). Applying a quasi-inverse and its unit and counit therefore identifies the mapping space from any object of $K_a$ into this vertex, up to equivalence, with a mapping space into $1_a$ in $I_a$. It is contractible, which is precisely finality in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This does not assume that $a$ is final in $C$.

The relative-join definition [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] supplies $J$, its inclusions and $j_c$. It is a quasicategory: apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-cartesian-realization] to $u^{\mathrm{op}}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse vertex order. This reverses the two ordered join blocks and identifies the opposite of $C^{\mathrm{op}}\star_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}K^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $J$. Reversal takes an inner horn of index $j$ to one of index $n-j$, so opposites of quasicategories are quasicategories.

Endpoint maps alone do not specify a map out of a join. We construct the mixed simplices and the required exact normalizations. An $n$-simplex $x$ of $J$ with initial block $[i]$ consists of an arrow prism $q:\Delta^1\times\Delta^i\to C$ and a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to C$ such that $q(1,-)=\sigma|_{[i]}$. The cases $i=-1,n$ are the pure $C,K$ cases. Let $P_x$ be the nerve of the poset with ordered lists $s_0,\ldots,s_i$ and $t_0,\ldots,t_n$, with cross relations $s_j\leq t_l$ exactly when $j\leq l$, and no relations from a $t$ to an $s$. Let $Q_x\subseteq P_x$ be the union of the prism on $s_0,\ldots,s_i,t_0,\ldots,t_i$ and the target simplex on all $t_l$. Evaluate these pieces by $q$ and $\sigma$, which agree on their common target face. Simplex operators send source and target vertices to source and target vertices at their image indices. Form $P,Q$ by taking these diagrams over all simplices of $J$ and identifying their simplex operators; this is a degreewise quotient of disjoint unions of sets, with its induced operators. Their evaluations give $Q\to C$. The chains
$$s_0<\cdots<s_i<t_{i+1}<\cdots<t_n$$
give a simplicial map $d:J\to P$; repeated indices give repeated vertices and hence degeneracies. For pure $K,C$ its evaluation is respectively source evaluation and the identity.

Prescribe additional values as follows. Let $H\subseteq J$ be the union of the images of $\delta\star1:A\star_C C\to J$ and all $j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}$. These are simplicial subsets: the first map is injective, and the prism comparison is injective because its prism contains a maximal chain mapping onto the full simplex $\Delta^{r+1}$. On a simplex in the first image evaluate $P_x$ by sending $s_j,t_j$ to vertex $j$ of $\sigma$. On a simplex in the second image, represented by a base slice simplex $\tau:\Delta^{i+1}\to C$ ending at $c$ followed by apex vertices, evaluate it by $s_j\mapsto j$ and $t_l\mapsto i+1$, followed by $\tau$. The formulas agree with $Q_x$. They agree on intersections: if an identity-arrow prism also has constant target, its source is constant with that same value, and the top chain in the slice prism forces $\tau$ to be constant. The pure-factor cases agree as well. These formulas commute with simplex operators, including operators discarding one block. Thus they define $Q\cup P_H\to C$, where $P_H$ is the image of the subdiagram supported on $H$.

Here is an inner-horn extension of this prescribed map to $P$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] for the unique nondegenerate representative of each supporting simplex, and [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] for the relative skeletal filtration of $H\subseteq J$. Filter $P$ by these support cells. The diagrams $P_x,Q_x$ and their prescribed maps commute with degeneracy operators; consequently degenerate supports add no cells. On attaching a support simplex, its proper faces have already been identified with the earlier support pieces, exactly as in that boundary-cell filtration. At a support $x$ discard chains in $Q_x$, in its support boundary, or in the already prescribed $P_H$. A remaining chain contains a source vertex and a target vertex with index greater than $i$. If $s_j$ is its last source vertex, pair the chain without $t_j$ with the chain obtained by inserting $t_j$. The inserted vertex is strictly between a source vertex and a later target. Both chains use the same set of supporting indices, since $s_j$ already carries index $j$; hence both or neither lie over a proper support face. Supports in $H$ are prescribed in full, and the same pairing therefore respects that subdiagram too. For a fixed support order pairs first by $j$, then by the dimension of the larger chain. Deleting the last source gives a chain with smaller last-source index, or a pure target chain in $Q_x$; deleting any other vertex except $t_j$ gives a smaller-dimensional paired chain, a support-boundary chain, or a chain in $Q_x$. Thus each larger chain attaches along the inner horn missing $t_j$, adding its paired face at the same time. This describes every remaining chain exactly once. The inclusion $Q\cup P_H\subseteq P$ is consequently a succession of inner-horn attachments. Fill those horns in $C$ using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], to obtain $F:P\to C$, and set $S=Fd$. The pure-factor formulas give $Si_K=\pi$, $Si_C=1_C$. The prescribed slice pieces give $Sj_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}=k_c$ on all simplices, and the identity-arrow pieces give
$$S(\delta\star1)(\epsilon,\sigma)=\sigma.$$
These are exact equalities, with no choice of composition left on these prescribed subdiagrams.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, map S; agent-written normalized inner-horn construction expanding the omitted mixed-simplex details.

proof.text:
The simplicial map $\delta$ sends every simplex of $A$ to its prism constant in the arrow direction. The induced relative-join formula of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], applied to $A\star_A A=\Delta^1\times A$, defines $\beta$. Its endpoints are $i_K\delta$ and $i_C|_A$, and the last equation of step 4 makes $S\beta$ constant. Since $A$ is full, $A\star_C C$ identifies with the full simplicial subset of $\Delta^1\times C$ whose vertices over $0$ lie in $A$. Thus $(b,k_c)$ factors through it and defines $T_c$. Define $\gamma_c^+$ on $\Delta^1\times I_c^{\triangleright}$ by sending $(t,w)$ to
$$(\max\{t,b(w)\},k_c(w))\in A\star_C C$$
and then applying $\delta\star1$. Maximum is monotone, so this is a simplicial map. At $t=0,1$ it gives $T_c,T_c^+$. Its base-vertex component is $\beta_a$ and its apex component is the identity.

For $\gamma_c^-$, an $n$-simplex of $\Delta^1\times I_c^{\triangleright}$ consists of $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$ and a cone simplex with base indices $0,\ldots,r$, represented by $\tau:\Delta^{r+1}\to C$ ending at $c$, and apex indices $r+1,\ldots,n$. For $r=-1$, send it to the constant simplex $i_C(c)$. Otherwise its image in $J$ has the same cut $r$. Its initial $K$-simplex is the arrow prism $\tau\rho$, where
$$\rho(t,j)=\begin{cases}r+1&t=1\text{ and }\epsilon(j)=1,\\ j&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad t\in[1],\ j\in[r].$$
Its target-coordinate simplex is $\tau\nu$, where $\nu(j)=j$ if $j\leq r$ and $\epsilon(j)=0$, and $\nu(j)=r+1$ otherwise; its final $C$-block is constant at $c$. Both indexing maps are monotone, and the target of the prism equals the initial face of $\tau\nu$, so this is an actual relative-join simplex. For a simplex operator $\alpha$, let $\bar\alpha$ be its restriction on retained base vertices extended by sending the new slice apex to the old apex. The identities $\bar\alpha\rho_{\epsilon\alpha}=\rho_\epsilon(1\times\alpha)$ on the base prism and $\bar\alpha\nu_{\epsilon\alpha}=\nu_\epsilon\alpha$ on the target coordinates follow in the two cases $\epsilon\alpha=0,1$. They also hold when the operator discards the base or apex block. Thus the formulas commute with faces and degeneracies. At constant $\epsilon=0$ the initial arrows are identities and the target coordinate is $k_c$, giving $T_c$; at constant $\epsilon=1$ they are the slice-diagonal prism and constant target $c$, giving $T_c^-$. This is a coherent transformation by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. At $e:a\to c$ its square has source side $1_a$ and target side $e$, so its image under $\pi$ is $1_a$. At the apex it is constant. This gives all asserted components together with their higher compatibility data.
